title: Decimate Sequence
cap_description: Keep one item out of every N from an input sequence (drop the rest)
documentation:
## Purpose

Reduces the length of a sequence by keeping items at positions `0, N, 2N, ...` and dropping the rest. Useful for sub-sampling a long sequence — e.g. taking every 10th frame from `extract-frames`, every 5th record from a CSV, every Nth file from a folder.

## Inputs

- A sequence of any media type.
- An optional integer stride `N` (default: `1`, which is identity passthrough).

## Outputs

A sequence of the same media type as the input, containing approximately `ceil(input_count / N)` items. Per-item metadata on each kept item passes through unchanged.

## Notes

- The cap is generic over media (`in = media:`, `out = media:`); the planner routes it for any sequence input. The output's media URN matches the input's exactly — items themselves are passed through, not re-encoded.
- `--keep-every 1` (or omitting the argument) is exact passthrough.
- Negative, zero, or non-integer values fail loudly rather than silently being treated as 1; this is by design — a misspelled flag should surface, not be papered over.
- An empty input sequence is treated as a real input error (not a "successfully decimated zero items" success), since silently emitting an empty sequence would let downstream caps run on nothing without anyone noticing.

args.arg_description: Stride N: keep one item out of every N. Positive integer. Omit for passthrough.

output.output_description: Decimated sequence (same media type as input)
